tetris.title: Tetris
tetris.description: A solo block puzzle with SRS rotation, 7-bag, hold and ghost pieces. Game-background shortcuts respect focused controls, and the on-screen pad works with keyboard and touch.

keyboard.title: Keyboard Controls
items: On the game background, Left/Right moves; hold to repeat.
On the game background, Up or X rotates clockwise; Z or Ctrl rotates counterclockwise.
On the game background, Down soft drops and Space hard drops.
On the game background, C or Shift holds.
On the game background, P or Escape pauses/resumes. Enter starts a game from the idle or game-over screen.
Focus an on-screen pad button and press Space or Enter to perform its labeled action once.
Game shortcuts do not intercept text fields, links, other buttons or IME composition.

touch.title: Touch Controls
items: Tap the board to rotate clockwise.
Drag left or right across the board to move by cells.
Drag down slowly to soft drop, or flick down to hard drop.
Flick up to hold.
Hold the on-screen left, right or down button to repeat movement.
Pause, a new game or leaving the page clears held controls. Use a fresh input after resuming.

scoring.title: Scoring System
items: Single 100 · Double 300 (× level)
Triple 500 · Tetris 800 (× level)
T-Spin Single 800 · Double 1200 · Triple 1600
Back-to-back (Tetris/T-Spin in a row) ×1.5
Combo: 50 × combo × level per consecutive clear
Level up every 10 lines; speed increases with level

whatIs.title: What is Tetris?
whatIs.description: Move and rotate falling pieces to complete horizontal lines. Solo mode keeps hold, a five-piece preview, a ghost, levels and existing scoring. Keyboard shortcuts are separated from focused buttons, links and text fields.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Start solo play with the Start button.
Use shortcuts on the game background, or Tab to a pad button and activate it with Space or Enter.
On touch screens, use pad buttons and board gestures. The ghost shows where the piece will land.
Pause when needed. After resuming, press movement keys or buttons again.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Watch the ghost piece (translucent preview) to see exactly where your piece will land.
Save the I-piece (long bar) for a Tetris — clearing four lines at once — for maximum points.
Keep your stack as flat as possible; irregular peaks make it increasingly hard to place pieces as speed increases.

items.q: Does Space hard drop when a button is focused?
items.a: A focused pad button performs its own labeled action once. Game shortcuts also leave the normal behavior of other buttons, links and text fields intact.

items.q: Can I mix keyboard and touch controls?
items.a: Yes. Inputs holding the same direction are tracked separately, so releasing one keeps another held input active. If opposite directions are held, the most recently pressed direction takes priority.
Press C or Shift on the game background, or use the hold control. Store the current piece and switch to the next one. Swapping is allowed once per piece.

items.q: Can an old touch carry over after pausing?
items.a: Pause, a new game, a hidden tab or loss of window focus clears held inputs and gestures. Releasing an old pointer after resuming does not apply an action to the new game.
